svg.title: Lakehouse Delta Optimization: Choosing V-Order, Optimized Write, Deletion Vectors, or Compaction
svg.desc: A decision tree starting from a table's dominant workload pattern. Read-heavy tables branch to V-Order; write-heavy streaming/ingestion tables branch to Optimized Write; tables with frequent row-level updates or deletes branch to deletion vectors; all tables converge on a periodic compaction question, which branches into Auto Compaction for tables under 1 GB and scheduled OPTIMIZE plus Auto Compaction for larger tables. A warning node covers the trap of enabling deletion vectors without periodic OPTIMIZE, which measurably degrades read performance.
svg.text: Fabric Lakehouse: Delta Optimization Decision Guide
Choose the right optimization strategy for each layer and workload pattern

g.aria-label: What is this table's dominant pattern?
g.title: What is this table's dominant pattern? — The root question: route by how the table is actually read and written, not by habit.
g.text: What is the dominant workload pattern?

svg.text: Avoids 15% write penalty on every job
Check: no COPY Activity on this table

g.title: Enable V-Order — Write-time Parquet reorganization that speeds up downstream reads across Fabric engines.

svg.text: Only affects future writes (not existing files)
Run OPTIMIZE to rewrite existing files

g.title: Auto Compaction alone — Automatic post-write compaction sufficient for tables under roughly 1 GB.
Is the table under ~1 GB? — The convergence point: every optimization path still needs periodic compaction, sized to table volume.
Auto Compaction + scheduled OPTIMIZE — Larger tables need Auto Compaction paired with a periodic OPTIMIZE pass targeting 500 MB–1 GB files.
Enable Optimized Write — Shuffles data across executors before writing so each partition lands in fewer, larger files.

svg.text: best runtime + file stability in benchmarks

g.title: Trap: deletion vectors without OPTIMIZE — Unmerged deletion-vector markers accumulate and measurably slow reads until compaction runs.
Consider deletion vectors — Converts row-level UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE into a small marker file instead of a full-file rewrite.
g.text: After OPTIMIZE, deletion-vector and copy-on-write tables show identical read performance. Regular OPTIMIZE eliminates the merge-on-read overhead.
